judged_text: Salesforce is wired to parseRefreshTokenResponse but bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, so when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set Salesforce still refreshes with its own local client secrets and never uses the sync endpoint, unlike every other app in this diff. Self-hosters running the credential-sync deployment get inconsistent behavior: Salesforce credentials refresh locally with keys the child deployment may not have (client secrets unset -> consumer_key/client_secret empty strings -> Salesforce returns 400 on every refresh), breaking Salesforce only in the sync configuration this PR introduces.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the token refresh flow is hard-coded to `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token"...)` using `consumer_key`/`consumer_secret`, and it never calls the newly introduced `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` helper that switches to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true. Other integrations in this diff were updated to use `refreshOAuthTokens` for refreshes. Therefore, even when `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is configured, Salesforce will still refresh locally instead of via the sync endpoint, producing inconsistent and potentially broken behavior under the new credential-sync configuration.
